Campaign targeting and bidding - Amazon Ads


Campaign targeting and bidding
Keyword match types
Manual keyword targeting supports three match types. Broad match reaches
shopping queries that contain all the keyword terms in any order, including
close variations. Phrase match requires the query to contain the exact
phrase or close variations, in order. Exact match requires the query to
match the keyword or its close variations exactly.
Product targeting
Product targeting lets you target specific ASINs or entire categories.
Category targets can be refined by brand, price range, and star rating.
Negative targeting
Negative keywords, in exact and phrase form, prevent ads from matching
unwanted queries. Negative product targeting excludes specific ASINs or
brands.
Dynamic bidding
Three bidding strategies are available for Sponsored Products. Dynamic
bids down only lowers your bid in real time when a click is less likely to
convert. Dynamic bids up and down can raise your bid by up to 100% for
placement at the top of the first page of shopping results, and by up to
50% for all other placements, and lowers it when conversion is less
likely. Fixed bids use your exact bid without real-time adjustment.
Placement adjustments
You can additionally increase bids by placement, by up to 900%, for top
of search and product pages placements.
Campaign structure
Campaigns contain ad groups. Ad groups contain the ads and the keyword
or product targets that share a common theme. Daily budgets are set at the
campaign level, and portfolios group campaigns for organization and
budget caps.


New: budgets can now be set at portfolio level too.

Portfolios can carry a budget cap at the portfolio level.
